business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

stage_1.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and authorizing incorporation filings
stage_1.issuing_entity: Notary public in the subscriber's country of origin (or Panamanian notary if executed in Panama)
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country of origin is an Apostille member) or Consular Legalization via the nearest Panamanian consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporations Law of the Republic of Panama), as amended; relevant provisions for Sociedad Anónima, including Articles 1–52 and subsequent legislative reforms.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Microjurisdicción Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation), registered in the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under Panamanian law; share capital is authorized in the public deed and may be deferred. No escrow account or capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the Sole/Founding Shareholder of [COMPANY], S.A., that: (i) the share capital set forth in the Public Deed of Incorporation is hereby subscribed and fully accepted by the subscribers named therein, and the issuance of registered shares is approved; (ii) the registered office of the company is established at the address stated in the constitutional deed in Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the registered agent is engaged as required by law; (iii) the following persons are appointed to office: President, Treasurer and Secretary, each to serve until removed by law or shareholder resolution; (iv) the officers may execute all statutory filings, open corporate bank accounts, and engage payment processors necessary to conduct the company’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina de Nombres Mercantiles (Public Registry, Commercial Names Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic or written commercial name request to the Public Registry, either directly or through a Panamanian registered agent. The registry verifies that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate or commercial name. Upon approval, the name is reserved for a brief statutory period.
required_dossiers: Completed name search application form
Proposed corporate name in original Spanish format
Scanned copy of applicant passport or national identity document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, submit an alternative distinctive name or amend the proposed name with a new distinctive prefix and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública authorized in the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators or their court-authorized attorneys appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the corporate statutory deed. The deed must include the article of incorporation, share capital, directors and officers, registered agent, and corporate purpose. The notary reviews for formal legal completeness and authenticates the execution.
required_dossiers: Obtained name availability certificate
Passport or ID of each incorporator and director
Power of attorney, if an attorney acts on behalf of any incorporator
Proposed text of Articles of Incorporation in Spanish
Residential or commercial address and contact details for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial form is questioned, the incorporators may execute a corrective amendment deed before the same notary. Any statutory defect in the deed can be cured by republishing or reformatting the instrument prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Public Deed in the Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Public Registry, Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized public deed and the supporting fiscal payment evidence at the Public Registry's Mercantile Section. The registry performs substantive review of the deed for conformity with Panamanian corporate law, posts the registration, and issues the Ficha Mercantil (mercantile corporate record) and public registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Name availability certificate
Notary fee and Public Registry filing fee receipts
Completed registry submission and legal review form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a caution or objection, the attorney must submit an explanatory brief and, where applicable, a notarized correction annex addressing each noted deficiency within the registry's stated timeline (.g., addition of missing clauses or signature consistency).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Organization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate board of directors and Panamanian registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the preliminary board meeting pursuant to the statutory deed. Adopt the First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office confirmation, officer appointment, and authorization of bank and processor onboarding. Maintain the duly certified minutes in the corporate records book and issue share certificates in the stock ledger.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution in original
Share subscription list and capital contribution acknowledgment
Completed officer acceptance forms
Corporate records book and stock ledger to be legalized by the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry identifies missing legalization of corporate books, submit the books for respective certification. Any officer resignation or incompatible director role can be cured by a supplementary shareholder resolution appointing replacements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registry and Municipal Operating Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipality of Panama – Aviso de Operación through Panama Emprende
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, apply for the tax identification number (RUC/NIT) with the National Tax Administration, and submit a Municipal Aviso de Operación (Notice of Business Operation) to the respective municipality. For an ISIC 6201 SaaS helpdesk business, the aviso is administrative and does not require an industrial license. Obtain the official RUC certificate and municipal fiscal registration.
required_dossiers: Public Registry certificate of incorporation
Duly notarized corporate power and board resolution appointing the legal representative
Registered office address and lease or title evidence
Completed DGI tax registration form
Municipal aviso de operación application form and nominal operating fee evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned due to address or representative discrepancies, cure by filing a correction or a supplemental board resolution verifying the exact registered office and legal representation. Provide updated municipal proof of premises if required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 customer support helpdesk; no industrial manufacturing or physical production license is required. The relevant administrative body is the Municipality of Panama for the non-industrial Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating industrial license is mandated; the company only requires the municipal Aviso de Operación and standard corporate existence registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Subject to EIA – activity consists exclusively of office-based software and cloud customer support services, with no physical construction, alteration, or industrial process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emissions. If premise-based, comply with local municipal wastewater and solid-waste collection rules. Any incidental electronic waste (e.g., used hardware) must be handled through an authorized recycler. No additional environmental permits apply for routine SaaS operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and preventive occupancy certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá if the leased office is physically occupied; municipal structural and land-use compatibility clearance for the stated registered address; workplace health and safety registration of employees with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; official taxpayer portal and e-services available through https://www.mef.gob.pa/dgi and the SIT@2 Electronic Tax Services platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a Panamanian branch must first appoint a resident agent and, for tax purposes, a Panamanian legal representative/fiscal agent. The representative must submit to the DGI the original notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation and by-laws (translated into Spanish), a board resolution appointing the fiscal agent, the executed power of attorney, and the completed RUC registration form (Solicitud de Inscripción o Actualización del Registro Único de Contribuyente). The DGI will then issue a single RUC number that serves as both the income tax TIN and the ITBMS/VAT identification number. For a Panama-incorporated Sociedad Anónima, the process is initiated after the public deed is recorded in the Public Registry and the Aviso de Operación is obtained from the corresponding municipality. A foreign entity that merely exports services with no Panamanian-source activity should still register with the DGI through the fiscal representative so that it may issue compliant export zero-rated invoices and sustain any ITBMS input credit claim. The DGI does not conduct a substantive review before issuing the RUC, but the completed file must include full beneficial ownership information under Panama's tax information and AML standards.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box or entity classification election comparable to the United States. A Sociedad Anónima is automatically a separate taxpaying corporation subject to entity-level taxation on Panamanian-source income only. There are no hybrid mismatch elections available under Panamanian domestic law; characterization follows legal form and source rules. Administrative elections are limited to the optional simplified small-taxpayer regime for low-turnover taxpayers, the selection of a fiscal agent for nonresident taxpayers, and the voluntary general regime for taxpayers below the small-taxpayer threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's form of VAT/GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 0 / no de minimis exemption under the standard ITBMS regime: registration is mandatory from the first habitual taxable transaction of goods or services in Panamanian territory. A simplified small-taxpayer regime may apply for gross annual revenue below approximately PAB 300,000, but that regime does not exempt a foreign or domestic supplier from obtaining an RUC or from issuing valid electronic invoices when a taxable supply is made.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has implemented mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI's Factura Electrónica system. Registered taxpayers must issue invoices in an approved XML/JSON electronic format through the DGI portal, direct API integration, or a DGI-authorized technology service provider. Invoices must contain the DGI-assigned validation code and a QR code or digital thumbprint, evidencing real-time receipt and fiscal clearance by the DGI. Once the electronic authorization is obtained, paper folios issued by the DGI are no longer valid for standard ITBMS taxpayers. Foreign suppliers with a Panamanian RUC must likewise transmit all invoices through the same mechanism. Invoicing without the DGI-validated code may result in the invoice being treated as a null document for the buyer's input credit and may expose the issuer to fines and surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The ITBMS is zero-rated on exports of goods physically departing Panamanian customs territory and on exportation of services rendered outside Panama or supplied for the exclusive benefit of a non-resident recipient. For the target helpdesk and conversational-bot cloud activity, zero-rating requires (i) a contractual recipient that is not a Panamanian resident or a Panamanian permanent establishment, (ii) the service to be performed principally from servers or personnel located outside Panama or delivered into the recipient's foreign environment, (iii) no actual use or consumption of the service by the Panamanian exporter or any Panamanian establishment, and (iv) commercial and banking evidence that the consideration is collected in foreign currency or through an international payment rail such as Stripe or PayPal. Invoicing a foreign customer alone is not sufficient; the taxpayer must maintain service-level documentation, IP addresses or delivery logs, and an executed export services contract demonstrating that the place of use and economic benefit is outside Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana - DUA) accepted and sealed by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading for ocean freight or Air Waybill for air freight showing the Panamanian exporter as shipper and a foreign consignee
Commercial invoice issued in English or Spanish describing the goods, HS code, Incoterms, and export value
Packing list and, where applicable, export permit or sanitary/phytosanitary certificate
Proof of payment and Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement evidencing collection from the foreign buyer within the repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA electronically cross-match export declarations, e-invoices, and bank inflows. If an exporter claims zero-rating for a supply that is recharacterized as domestic or locally consumed, the DGI will assess ITBMS at 7% on the gross amount plus statutory interest from the invoice date. Penalties can reach up to 100% of the omitted tax, plus fines for false invoicing and failure to maintain supporting documentation, and reckless or fraudulent claims may trigger criminal fiscal-fraud proceedings under the Código Fiscal. Retroactive clawback generally covers open tax periods under Panamanian prescription rules, and the taxpayer must then correct all affected VAT credit balances and customer invoices.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), acting together with the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) on monetary-fiscal policy coordination. The Republic of Panama maintains no formal central bank; the United States Dollar is unlimited legal tender, and the Panamanian Balboa exists solely as a divisional coin at a fixed 1:1 peg. The SBP therefore performs banking conduct, solvency, liquidity, and Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) supervision rather than traditional central-bank lender-of-last-resort or currency-issue functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The regime is one of full and unrestricted convertibility across both current and capital accounts. With complete official dollarization, there is no Panamanian exchange-control authority, no surrender or repatriation obligation, no prior import authorization, and no central-bank approval for capital inflows or profit remittances. Dividends, branch profits, and royalties may be remitted freely by wire to any jurisdiction, subject only to standard commercial-bank documentary scrutiny, the bank's internal AML/CFT classification, and compliance with Panama's territorial income-tax rules regarding the source of income. A practical remittance hurdle is the availability of clear underlying invoices or audited-reserve evidence that establishes the non-Panamanian source of the revenue, thereby confirming the absence of 10% dividend withholding (which applies only to Panamanian-source profits). Non-resident shareholders face no capital-gains tax on disposal of shares in a Panama S.A., and no stamp duty applies to remittance documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. A Panamanian exporter of SaaS/helpdesk support services may lawfully retain USD receivables in offshore bank accounts, provided the income is formally reported to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under the territorial principle and reflected in the corporate books and annual tax return. Export of services by the PA_CORP helpdesk entity is exempt from Panamanian value-added tax (ITBMS at 7%) when the service is actually used or exploited abroad; there is no foreign-exchange certificate, no surrender requirement, and no requirement to liquidate proceeds into Balboa or any other currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta de Depósito a la Vista) and Capital Escrow Account for public-sector contracting; government fiscal-agent bank
Operational Account (Corriente / Cuenta de Operaciones) and segregated Capital Escrow Account for paid-in capital verification
Operational USD account with transactional payments module and segregated Escrow Account for capital contributions
Operational Account oriented to fintech, regtech, and digital-service exporters, with segregated Escrow in Foreign-Corporate Services division
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account; supportive of cross-border wire-heavy disbursement profiles
Operational Account and USD Term Deposit for liquidity buffer; corporate account opening subject to global OFAC and source-of-funds requirements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. Offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs), including Airwallex, Wise Business, Dukascopy-side platforms, and other non-bank payment switching providers, have no legally recognized depository status in Panama; the SBP's exclusive banking-license perimeter prevents an unlicensed EMI from receiving Panamanian deposits or acting as the primary clearing institution. However, such EMIs are practicable as secondary disbursement rails for contractor payouts and foreign-subsidiary expenses, provided the PA_CORP S.A. maintains its principal liquidity in an SBP-regulated bank. For inbound merchant acquiring, Stripe and PayPal are viable but operate through overseas acquiring sponsors, requiring the Panamanian entity to effect settlement through its own SBP-regulated bank account; direct onshore payment-institution licensing by the SBP (Reglamento de Banca Digital / sandbox) is optional, yet operationally unnecessary for a Low_Risk_Standard SaaS helpdesk scope. Legal constraints include FATF Recommendation 16 transparency expectations, the prohibition on bearer-style anonymity, and the need to ensure that any EMI-associated Mastercard/Visa virtual corporate card is backed by a customer-funded account at an SBP-regulated bank rather than an unlicensed PSP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the standard Panama S.A. with non-resident shareholders, Tier-1 banks generally require at least one director or the company's legal representative (Residente Legal) to appear physically for an on-site identity verification interview at account opening, in accordance with SBP AML/CFT regulations (Law 23 of 2015, Decree 13-2015, and SBP Acuerdo 03-2018). Fully remote onboarding is the exception rather than the rule: it is granted only where the ultimate beneficial owner already holds a portfolio relationship with the bank or where the bank accepts notarized and apostilled resolutions combined with a supervised video-call interview in front of a licensed notary of a recognized common-law jurisdiction. For a helpdesk/SaaS entity without local payroll, banks will require documented substance evidence, including a physical registered-office lease, a Panamanian legal representative with personal presence, and the original board resolution authorizing each signatory. Practical mandate: shortest onboarding path = legal representative attending in person with original passport, certified copy of the Sociedad Anónima public deed, updated Certificate of Registry of the Registro Público, electronical share register, and a draft board resolution in Spanish.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customer-base exposure to sanctioned, high-risk, or unverifiable jurisdictions: cloud helpdesk subscriptions originated from countries under OFAC/UN sanctions or from high-risk tax-haven-adjacent geographies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated customer screening output (Dow Jones/Refinitiv/Wolfsberg-style PEP-and-Sanctions scan) for every onboarded merchant client; geolocation verification evidence from the SaaS platform; a written compliance policy disclaiming service to sanctioned or FATF-listed jurisdictions; a Panamanian external AML opinion letter; and a representation by the board that no jurisdictional re-routing of subscriptions is permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Volumetric mismatch between claimed low-risk SaaS operations and observed monthly wire velocity or accumulation of unexplained treasury inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured order-to-cash register with counterparty legal names, tax identifiers, and country codes; executed Master Subscription Agreements evidencing per-seat pricing; third-party cloud-infrastructure invoices (compute, telephony, AI-model API spend) matching operating scale; and internally prepared financial statements under NIIF for SMEs, certified by the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: use of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), bearer-share historical exposures, or undisclosed nominee directors creating layered control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated electronical share register in Panama (Law 52 of 2016 abolishes bearer shares); a communications and control map identifying all intermediate foundations or nominee vehicles; a certified legal opinion by Panamanian counsel naming each ultimate beneficial owner; and revoked pro-forma powers of attorney, ensuring clean UBO record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid in-and-out fund movement without transactional substance, a classic conduit-risk pattern detected by SBP transaction-monitoring rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward projection of treasury cycle showing 3-5% operating margin; supporting supplier invoices for every outbound disbursement; traceable STRIPE/PAYPAL merchant settlement reports; bank statement continuity of at least six months and an explanation of any same-day investments or zero-day liquidity sweeps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office substance red flag: a registered S.A. without physical employees, IT equipment, or demonstrated helpdesk delivery capability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Domiciliation lease contract for the registered office; contract for local legal-representation services; helpdesk shift schedule, staff employment or BPO agreements with named agents; evidence of SIM/phone-lines, ticketing tools, and cloud server estate; and local payment data showing Panamanian operating expenditures (legal fees, representation, minor utilities).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing should use a SWIFT MT103 message with UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) and DCBR-style ordering-customer detail. The transferer's bank credits the Panamanian beneficiary account through the bank's U.S. correspondent (usually via CHIPS or Fedwire at the Fed funds layer where the Panamanian bank maintains a USD nostro in New York). The beneficiary fields must reflect exactly the name of the Sociedad Anónima registered in the Registro Público, its full address, the beneficiary bank's BIC, and the local account number (Panama has no IBAN system, so the full account number and optional CLABE-style internal code are required). In Field 70-77 'Remittance Information', the investor must insert a precise purpose narrative: 'Aporte de capital social / Capital contribution to paid-in shares', referencing the specific board resolution approving the subscription. The assisting bank may request a certified copy of the shareholder resolution, an updated share register, and, for statistics, an indication that the transaction qualifies as 'Inversión Directa' (direct investment equity) rather than debt, thereby avoiding the 5% withholdings payable on intercompany debt interest remitted abroad under the territorial Income Tax Code. No prior Central-Bank approval or exchange-control declaration is required; however, the receiving Panamanian bank will perform an OFAC/FATF screening of the sending institution. For intra-LatAm parent funding, the transfer should also include the country-level tax ID (RUC or equivalent) of the payer to permit the receiving bank to classify the transaction cleanly within its automated BOP reporting framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements for the PA_CORP helpdesk entity should be effected primarily via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for supplier payments, contractor remuneration, and overseas software licensing, applying the charge option RIP (shared-cost or beneficiary-charges as negotiated). For larger capital-equipment or infrastructure purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit governed by UCP600) may be issued by the Panamanian corporate bank through its trade-finance desk, typically confirmed by an international correspondent bank, with the beneficiary's documents including original commercial invoice, bill of lading/AWB, inspection certificates, and insurance vouchers; for SaaS the LC is rarely required. Day-to-day merchant receipts from Stripe Billing and PayPal are cleared into the settlement account via pooled USD settlement (Stripe/PayPal sponsor banks) then transferred to the Panamanian operational account by wire on a T+1 or T+2 cadence; the PA_CORP entity must reconcile the Stripe/PayPal fees against its DGI export-service exemption and maintain valid customer evidence for every disbursement. For high-frequency contractor payouts, treasury may batch through Wise or an SBP-regulated remittance company, but final disbursements for payments traversing Panamanian banking law must remain visible to the SBP-regulated primary account to preserve auditability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) with licensed Panamanian banks or their international treasuries for converting excess USD into forecast EUR/GBP operational expense peaks

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) executed offshore through investment-grade non-resident counterparties to synthetically convert USD funding into target-currency liabilities where a local Panamanian bank lacks a direct swap book

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible Latin American currencies (ARS, PEN, VES; NDFs against COP/BRL available offshore) used solely to hedge regional helpdesk vendor payables, settled in USD, and fully permissible given the absence of Panamanian OTC derivative regulation
Interest-rate swaps (IRS) combined with USD borrowings to transform floating-rate exposure into fixed-rate certainty within the SBP's prudential asset-liability management expectations

Structured FX participating forwards or collars provided by an SBP-regulated bank's treasury desk for multi-year SaaS contract receivables denominated in EUR, provided the instrument does not breach the entity's territorial-source income filing position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax — Tasa Única Anual (Flat Tax) for Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, via PanamaTax portal or Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July; standard minimum-capital S.A. assessed at USD 300
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late charge of 10% of the tax plus monthly interest; persistent non-payment for three consecutive years permits the Registro Público to dissolve and cancel the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return — Declaración de Renta (Form 120) for legal entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), PanamaTax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year S.A., on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax plus annual interest; continued failure or deliberate non-filing can lead to criminal tax sanctions and suspension of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration — Declaración de Beneficiario Final and Share-Transfer Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Legal Entities Registry / UBO electronic module, filed through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the incorporation anniversary; within 15 business days after any share transfer or change of beneficial owner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registered agent may be fined and the company may be denied certificates of good standing; the Registro Público may suspend the entity's legal existence during continued breach.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance of statutory corporate registers and minute books at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident agent / registered office in Panama; notarised filings to Registro Público only when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each annual general meeting if one is held, and immediately upon each share transfer, director change, or resolution requiring register endorsement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct registry sanction for ordinary private records, but defective registers may invalidate share transfers, impair legal standing, and expose the resident agent to AML compliance liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for a standard private S.A. unless the entity is a regulated financial institution, insurance company, securities issuer, or is expressly required by DGI, the banking supervisor, or the securities regulator. An audit may also be required by a financing institution or by the foreign parent's consolidated reporting rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS and IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the Panamanian Accounting Technical Board; no separate commercial general-purpose Panamanian GAAP applies to standard S.A. entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must collect and retain UBO information and file an annual confirmatory declaration with the Registro Público on the corporate anniversary. Any share transfer, issuance of bearer shares, or change of control must be reported within 15 business days. Bearer shares must be immobilised with a licensed custodian and the beneficial owner identified to the resident agent before the transfer is completed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (Registro de Acciones)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) of Shareholders and Board of Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 7,500 per year for an optional or triggered audit of a standard S.A.

stage_6.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) issued by DGI; entering a zero/foreign TIN makes the filing void.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not enter their home-country IDs; the Panamanian S.A. must obtain a Panama RUC through a registered tax agent before filing.
